article_title: Free bus travel for disabled people in England to be extended to 24 hours a day

tasks.prompt: What is the main change announced in the article?
options: Eligible disabled people in England will be able to use their free bus passes at any time of day
All bus travel in the UK will become free for every passenger
Disabled bus passes will be limited to weekend journeys
Local councils will stop issuing disabled bus passes
tasks.correct_answer: Eligible disabled people in England will be able to use their free bus passes at any time of day
tasks.explanation_hebrew: השינוי המרכזי הוא הרחבת השימוש בכרטיסי הנסיעה החינמיים של זכאים עם מוגבלות באנגליה לכל שעות היממה.

tasks.prompt: When is the nationwide 24-hour entitlement due to begin?
options: Immediately in August 2026
1 April 2027
1 January 2030
Only after each council holds a referendum
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ההרחבה הארצית אמורה להתחיל ב־1 באפריל 2027, לאחר השלמת האישור וההיערכות.

tasks.prompt: What are the current standard weekday hours for these passes in England?
options: Midnight to 6am
6am to noon
9:30am to 11pm
Weekdays are completely excluded
tasks.explanation_hebrew: כיום ההסדר הארצי הרגיל מאפשר שימוש בימי חול בין 9:30 בבוקר ל־11 בלילה, אלא אם רשות מקומית מממנת הרחבה.

tasks.prompt: Why does the article describe buses as a “lifeline”?
options: They are used only during emergencies
They replace every form of healthcare
They are the longest vehicles on the road
They provide an essential connection to work, education, healthcare and daily life
tasks.correct_answer: They provide an essential connection to work, education, healthcare and daily life
tasks.explanation_hebrew: lifeline הוא דבר חיוני שמאפשר לאנשים לקיים את חיי היומיום; כאן האוטובוסים מחברים לעבודה, לימודים, טיפול רפואי ושירותים.

tasks.prompt: How much funding is being provided for the change?
options: £6 million
£60 million
£600 million
No public funding
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ליישום השינוי הוקצו 60 מיליון ליש״ט מתקציבי ממשלה קיימים.

tasks.prompt: What does the “postcode lottery” refer to in the article?
options: A prize draw held on buses
A system for registering vehicle numbers
Unequal support depending on where a disabled person lives
A discount available only by post
tasks.correct_answer: Unequal support depending on where a disabled person lives
tasks.explanation_hebrew: postcode lottery מתאר מצב שבו רמת הסיוע תלויה באזור המגורים, משום שחלק מהרשויות מימנו שעות נוספות ואחרות לא.

tasks.prompt: Give three ways the 24-hour pass could benefit disabled people.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שלושה יתרונות מעשיים המתוארים בכתבה.
expected_points: Access to work or training before 9:30am
Easier travel to education
Better access to healthcare appointments
Lower transport costs
Greater independence and dignity
Reduced isolation and easier participation in community life

tasks.prompt: Summarise the old rules, the new entitlement and how the change will be funded.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: הסיכום צריך לכלול את שעות ההסדר הקודם, מועד השינוי, היקפו ומקור המימון.
expected_points: The standard weekday entitlement was limited to 9:30am–11pm
Some councils already paid for wider local access
From 1 April 2027 eligible disabled pass holders will have 24-hour use
The policy applies across England where the pass is valid
The £60m cost is split between the Department for Work and Pensions and the Department for Transport

tasks.prompt: Why does removing the time restriction also remove a barrier to employment?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לקשור בין שעות תחילת העבודה לבין אי־היכולת להשתמש בכרטיס לפני 9:30.
expected_points: Many jobs or training courses begin before 9:30am
A restricted pass could force a disabled worker to pay for the morning journey
Extra disability-related costs can make paid travel harder to afford
Twenty-four-hour validity makes commuting more predictable
Equal access can widen realistic work opportunities

tasks.prompt: Using the article, explain whether nationwide rules are fairer than allowing each council to choose the hours. Give two reasons and one possible implementation challenge.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג עמדה מנומקת, שני יתרונות של אחידות ארצית ואתגר יישום אחד.
expected_points: National rules end unequal treatment based on postcode
All eligible disabled people receive the same basic entitlement
The change supports independence, work, education and healthcare
Local transport authorities need time to prepare
Parliamentary approval and funding arrangements must be completed
The conclusion should weigh fairness against practical implementation
